# cache

Every cache, each with a budget: RAM frame cache, GPU texture cache, disk render cache, proxies, thumbnails, waveforms and loudness readings. Least-recently-used items are dropped first.

Every file kept on disk is named by the recording's fingerprint through `naming::stem`, the one place that turns a fingerprint into a file name. The fingerprint comes from a project file, which anyone can write, so only one of the form the app makes is accepted (the size, and a hash of exactly 32 hexadecimal digits); for any other (a `/`, `..`, an empty hash) a store reads nothing and writes nothing: it is simply not cached.

## Status

Phase 4 in progress: waveforms, clip thumbnails and proxies are done (frames kept on the graphics card are `engine::frames`). The frame cache in memory and the disk render cache come next; the timeline's cache bar (`ui_kit::timeline::cache_bar`) is where they will show what is ready.

## Files

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `src/waveform.rs` | `peaks(path, stream)`: the loudest sample in each 1/100 s of a sound stream, and its highest and lowest (`up`, `down`: the wave's shape above and below the middle), read once on a worker at the stream's own rate (a 20-minute stream is 120,000 numbers, kept in memory). `peaks_of_streams`: several streams of a file in one pass over it (`media::AudioStreams`). `Store`: peaks kept on disk by the recording's fingerprint and stream, 16 bits a number, three numbers a stretch (a three-hour stream is about 6 MB; a file of the first version, the loudest alone, is read again), the least recently used trimmed to a budget; `clear` removes them all. `peaks_as_read` hands the peaks over a few seconds of sound at a time while reading, for progress and for drawing the waveform as it fills in, and can be stopped |
| `src/proxy.rs` | Proxies (`docs/research/caching.md`, step 3). `Shelf`: the folder of proxies in the app's cache folder, one per recording and picture stream, named by the file's fingerprint (`file_for`), shared by the interface and the preview worker: the mode (`ProxyMode`: Off, On, Auto, a setting) and a counter that changes whenever a proxy comes or goes (`generation`) are atomics. `ready` (one that is built and not being deleted), `build` (writes `media::proxy` to a file of its own and puts it in place when complete; a stopped build is `Built::Stopped`, not an error), `used` (a proxy's last use is its file's time of change), `delete` (no longer offered at once; the file goes as soon as no preview has it open), `trim` (drops the ones used longest ago, never the open project's, to stay inside a budget in bytes; removes builds, and writes of `cleared.txt`, a program left behind), `usage` (bytes and count, of some proxies or all) and `clear` (removes some proxies or all, as `delete` does, waiting for a preview to let go; clearing all also removes builds left behind; only proxy files are ever touched; returns a `Cleared`: what went, where, and why some proxy could not). A proxy cleared on purpose is remembered for good in `cleared.txt` in the folder (one proxy name a line, written whole and put in place): `is_cleared` says so, so it is not built again by itself; `delete` sets the same mark (deleted on purpose); `build` and `unmark_cleared` take it off. `judge`: whether Auto builds one for a file, from its longest stretch between key frames and 30 frames' decoding timed here: over 50 ms for a typical jump, it does. Proxies belong to recordings, not projects, so they are not in `project::side_files` `build` takes how many stretches to build a file in, side by side (`media::proxy::write`). |
| `src/thumbs.rs` | `Store`: strips kept on disk by the recording's fingerprint and stream, each picture a JPEG (quality 85, a few hundred kilobytes a recording), with how they were taken (exact or not); `load`, `save`, covers beside them (`load_cover`, `save_cover`), `trim` to a budget (used longest ago first), `clear`. `cover(path, stream, …)`: the one picture a Library card rests on (`resting_moment`, a third of the way in on a picture of the strip), read on its own in tens of milliseconds, the key frame there when one is close. `strip(path, stream, …)` (the decoder opened once for a long recording's key frames): small pictures (fitted into 160×90) every 2 s or more along a video file, at most 300 per file, for drawing inside clips; tells its progress after each picture. Where the key frames are at most half the pictures' spacing apart (a long recording), each picture is the key frame nearest its moment, one frame decoded per picture (about 40 times quicker on a recording with key frames 4 s apart), unless `exact` is asked for |
| `src/disk.rs` | What the stores on disk share: `touch` (a kept file's last use is its time of change) and `trim(folder, extensions, budget)` (removes the files with those endings used longest ago until the rest fit the budget; a budget of 0 clears them; temporary files of writes a crash cut short (`diag::disk::temp_path`) go too once 10 minutes old, whatever the budget; nothing else in the folder is touched). The waveform and picture stores trim and clear with it, the loudness store clears with it (it has no budget) |
| `src/naming.rs` | `stem(fingerprint)`: `size-hash` for a fingerprint the app makes (`HASH_DIGITS` hexadecimal digits), `None` for any other; every store below names its files with it and treats `None` as "not cached" (the proxy shelf's `file_for` is `None` then, and `build` refuses with an explained error) |
| `src/loudness.rs` | `Store`: a file's loudness readings (`Reading`: gated loudness and true peak of each sound stream), a small text file per recording in the cache folder's `loudness/` (`loudness 1`, then a line per stream); `load` (only when every stream asked for is there), `save` (whole or not at all), `clear` (only its `.txt` files). The Library page measures (`library_page::loudness`) |
| `build.rs` | Linux debug builds: the tests find the fetched FFmpeg libraries |
